title: State of AI Usage
dek_2026: How many people and organisations use AI, how often, and for what: consumer assistant audiences (weekly and monthly, never mixed), organisational adoption, worker and adult usage surveys, what people actually ask ChatGPT, AI search reach, and China's AI-native app market, 2024 to 2026.

2024: OpenAI said ChatGPT had 300 million weekly active users in December 2024, up from 200 million in August 2024.
McKinsey's 2024 State of AI survey found that 78% of organisations used AI in at least one business function, up from 55% in 2023.
McKinsey found that 71% of organisations regularly used generative AI in at least one business function in 2024, more than double the 33% it recorded in 2023.
The St. Louis Fed's Real-Time Population Survey found that 44.6% of US adults aged 18 to 64 had used generative AI in August 2024, and 33.3% had used it for work.
Google said AI Overviews in Search reached more than 1 billion monthly users in October 2024, five months after their US launch.
2025: OpenAI said ChatGPT reached 800 million weekly active users in October 2025, double the 400 million it reported in February 2025.
McKinsey's 2025 State of AI survey, fielded in June and July 2025, found that 88% of organisations used AI in at least one business function, up from 78% a year earlier.
OpenAI's NBER study of 1.5 million ChatGPT conversations found that 73% of consumer messages were unrelated to work in June 2025, up from 53% in June 2024.
The St. Louis Fed's Real-Time Population Survey found that 54.6% of US adults aged 18 to 64 used generative AI in August 2025, up from 44.6% a year earlier.
Meta said its Meta AI assistant had about 1 billion monthly active users across its apps in May 2025, double the roughly 500 million it reported in September 2024.
2026: OpenAI said ChatGPT had more than 1 billion weekly active users on 31 August 2026, up from more than 900 million in February 2026.
Alphabet said the Gemini app had more than 1 billion monthly users on 28 October 2026, up from 750 million at the end of 2025.
QuestMobile counted 546 million monthly users of China's AI-native apps in September 2026, up 82.1% year on year, led by ByteDance's Doubao at 419 million.
Gallup found that 52% of US employees used AI at work at least a few times a year in May 2026, but only 15% used it daily.
McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, fielded in May and June 2026, found that 89% of organisations regularly used AI in at least one business function, against 88% in 2025.

2024: 2024 was the year AI assistants became mass-market products rather than curiosities. OpenAI said ChatGPT had 200 million weekly active users in August 2024 and 300 million by December 2024, and its paying base reached about 15.5 million subscribers by year-end, according to figures OpenAI gave shareholders, as reported by The Information. Google said AI Overviews in Search reached more than 1 billion monthly users in October 2024, and Meta said Meta AI had about 500 million monthly users in September 2024. Those two figures measure exposure inside products people already used, not people choosing an assistant, and they are monthly rather than weekly counts. They should not be placed beside ChatGPT's weekly figure as if they were the same quantity.

Inside organisations, 2024 was the inflection point. McKinsey's mid-2024 survey found that 78% of organisations used AI in at least one business function, up from 55% in 2023, and that 71% regularly used generative AI, up from 33%. These are self-reported shares of organisations with at least one use, so they measure breadth, not depth: a company running one chatbot pilot in marketing counts the same as one that has rebuilt its operations around AI. McKinsey's own surveys that year found few firms able to point to measurable earnings impact, which set up the question that dominated 2025: whether near-universal adoption was producing value or only activity.

Individual use was rising quickly but was still a minority habit. The St. Louis Fed's Real-Time Population Survey, run by Bick, Blandin and Deming, found that 44.6% of US adults aged 18 to 64 had used generative AI in August 2024 (restated from the 39.4% first published) and 33.3% had used it for work. Gallup found that 27% of US employees used AI at work at least a few times a year in the second quarter of 2024. Pew found that 23% of US adults had ever used ChatGPT in early 2024, rising to 43% among adults under 30. Microsoft's 2024 Work Trend Index put use at 75%, but it surveyed knowledge workers in 31 countries and is not comparable with the general-population surveys.
2025: 2025 was the year consumer AI use more than doubled and shifted towards everyday life. OpenAI reported ChatGPT at 400 million weekly active users in February 2025 and 800 million in October 2025. OpenAI's own study of 1.5 million conversations, published through NBER in September 2025, found that the share of consumer messages unrelated to work rose from 53% in June 2024 to 73% in June 2025, and that practical guidance, seeking information and writing made up roughly three-quarters of conversations. Programming was only about 4.2% of messages. The growth was not mainly professionals adopting a work tool; it was the general public using a general-purpose assistant for everyday questions, advice and editing their own text.

Competitors scaled mostly through distribution. Meta said Meta AI reached about 1 billion monthly users in May 2025, largely inside WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook. Google reported 750 million monthly Gemini app users at the end of 2025 and more than 2 billion monthly AI Overviews users in July 2025, and Microsoft reported 150 million monthly users across its Copilot apps in the quarter to September 2025. In China, QuestMobile counted 287 million monthly users of AI-native apps in September 2025; by December, Doubao had 226 million and DeepSeek 135 million, DeepSeek having fallen back from its January surge. These are monthly reach figures, which run well above weekly or daily engagement, and the per-app Chinese figures cannot be added together.

Organisational adoption approached saturation while worker-level use rose more slowly. McKinsey's 2025 survey, fielded in June and July, found that 88% of organisations used AI in at least one business function, yet only 39% attributed any EBIT impact to it. Among individuals, the St. Louis Fed survey found that 54.6% of US adults aged 18 to 64 used generative AI in August 2025 and 37.4% used it for work, while Gallup found that 46% of US employees used AI at work at least a few times a year by the fourth quarter and 23% used it a few times a week or more in the third. The gap between near-universal organisational adoption and frequent use by under a quarter of workers is the clearest sign of how shallow most deployments were.
2026: ChatGPT crossed the threshold OpenAI had been targeting. OpenAI said ChatGPT had more than 900 million weekly active users on 27 February 2026 and more than 1 billion on 31 August 2026, alongside more than 50 million paying subscribers reported in February. Growth has slowed in absolute terms: ChatGPT added about 400 million weekly users in the eight months from February to October 2025, but about 100 million in the six months from February to August 2026 (DERIVED from OpenAI's milestones). OpenAI cited 1.2 billion weekly users at its developer conference on 29 September 2026, but that figure may cover more than ChatGPT and its date is disputed, so it is not used as the ChatGPT count here.

Rivals are now at the same order of magnitude on their own measures. Alphabet said the Gemini app passed 1 billion monthly users on 28 October 2026, but that is a monthly count and is not directly comparable with ChatGPT's weekly figure. Meta has not given a 2026 Meta AI total, Microsoft gave only relative Copilot growth, and estimates for Claude range from 56 million to 245 million monthly users. China's AI-native apps reached 546 million monthly users in September 2026, according to QuestMobile, up 82.1% year on year, with Doubao at 419 million, Qwen at 158 million and DeepSeek at 122.65 million. Those app figures overlap, so they cannot be summed into a market total.

Worker use crossed half the workforce on the broadest measure but remains light for most. Gallup found that 52% of US employees used AI at work at least a few times a year in May 2026, 30% used it a few times a week or more, and 15% used it daily. The St. Louis Fed survey put generative AI use at 62% of US adults aged 18 to 64 and work use at 45% in May 2026. Pew found that 49% of US adults used AI chatbots in February 2026. McKinsey's 2026 survey found organisational adoption at 89%, essentially unchanged from 88%, while the share reporting any EBIT impact stayed at 37%. Breadth has plateaued; depth is the variable that is still moving.

Search is where most people meet AI without choosing it. Google's AI Overviews reached about 2.5 billion monthly users by May 2026, according to secondary reporting of Google I/O, and AI Mode passed 1 billion. Yet AI platforms still sent only about 0.32% of all website traffic in 2026, according to SE Ranking, up from 0.02% in 2024. ChatGPT's share of chatbot web visits fell to 53.9% in May 2026 on Similarweb's measure as Gemini grew to 27.9%. The pattern is consistent: AI is absorbing a large and growing share of questions, but it passes very little of that attention on to the open web, which changes what being visible online means for publishers.

takeaways_2026: ChatGPT passed 1 billion weekly active users on 31 August 2026 (OpenAI), but growth has slowed: about 100 million added in six months of 2026 against about 400 million in eight months of 2025 (DERIVED).

The Gemini app passed 1 billion monthly users on 28 October 2026 (Alphabet); a monthly count is not comparable with ChatGPT's weekly one, and Meta, Microsoft and Anthropic published no comparable 2026 consumer totals.
Organisational adoption has plateaued near the ceiling at 89% (McKinsey, mid-2026) while worker use is broad but light: 52% of US employees use AI at work at all, 15% daily (Gallup, May 2026).
China's AI-native apps reached 546 million monthly users in September 2026 (QuestMobile), up 82.1% year on year, led by Doubao at 419 million; per-app figures overlap and cannot be added.
yoy_takeaways: ChatGPT's weekly users grew from 300 million (December 2024) to 800 million (October 2025) to more than 1 billion (August 2026) — roughly 3.3x in under two years (DERIVED: 1,000M / 300M), with growth decelerating in 2026.
Organisational AI adoption rose from 78% (2024) to 88% (2025) to 89% (2026) in McKinsey's surveys: the big move was 2023 to 2025, and the 2026 change is within noise.

Individual use roughly doubled on every general-population measure: US employees using AI at work went from 27% (Q2 2024) to 46% (Q4 2025) to 52% (May 2026) in Gallup's survey, and US adults aged 18 to 64 using generative AI went from 44.6% (August 2024) to 54.6% (August 2025) to 62% (May 2026) in the St. Louis Fed's survey.

Use shifted from work to everyday life: the non-work share of ChatGPT consumer messages rose from 53% (June 2024) to 73% (June 2025) in OpenAI's NBER study, while AI's share of website referral traffic stayed below half a percent (0.02% in 2024, 0.24% in 2025, 0.32% in 2026, SE Ranking).

faq_2026.q: How many people use ChatGPT in 2026?
faq_2026.a: OpenAI said ChatGPT had more than 1 billion weekly active users on 31 August 2026, up from more than 900 million on 27 February 2026 and 800 million in October 2025. OpenAI also reported more than 50 million paying subscribers in February 2026. A figure of 1.2 billion weekly users cited at OpenAI's developer conference on 29 September 2026 may include other OpenAI products, and a figure of about 1 billion monthly app users (mid-2026) is a different metric.

faq_2026.q: Which AI assistant has the most users in 2026?
faq_2026.a: It depends on the metric, and the metrics should not be mixed. On weekly users, ChatGPT leads with more than 1 billion (OpenAI, 31 August 2026). On monthly users, Alphabet said the Gemini app passed 1 billion on 28 October 2026. Meta AI was put at about 1 billion monthly users in May 2025 but Meta has not given a 2026 total. In China, ByteDance's Doubao leads with 419 million monthly users in September 2026, according to QuestMobile.

faq_2026.q: What percentage of companies use AI in 2026?
faq_2026.a: McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, fielded from 4 May to 8 June 2026 among 1,719 respondents, found that 89% of organisations regularly use AI in at least one business function, against 88% in 2025 and 78% in 2024. Only 37% reported any EBIT impact from AI, so adoption is near-universal but measurable value is not.

faq_2026.q: What share of US workers use AI at work in 2026?
faq_2026.a: Gallup found that 52% of US employees used AI at work at least a few times a year in May 2026, 30% used it a few times a week or more, and 15% used it daily. The St. Louis Fed's Real-Time Population Survey found that 45% of US adults aged 18 to 64 used generative AI for work in May 2026. The two surveys use different questions and bases, so their figures differ.

faq_2026.q: What do people actually use ChatGPT for?
faq_2026.a: Mostly everyday, non-work tasks. OpenAI's NBER study of 1.5 million consumer conversations found that 73% of messages were unrelated to work in June 2025, up from 53% in June 2024. Practical guidance, seeking information and writing made up roughly three-quarters of messages; writing was 40% of work-related messages, mostly editing users' own text, and programming was only about 4.2% of all messages.
